correctness.rationale: Direct Euclidean projection distances give exact tie coordinates s and -1−√2, the two-step return R(t)=(1−|t|)/2, and a complete three-case pullback partition. The return on the positive invariant interval has four-step contraction (1+t)/4, proving the unique four-cycle and all global basins. Interval lengths sum to 14(2−√2), and boundary normalization simplifies exactly to 6−4√2. Poincaré recurrence identifies the six ergodic invariant probabilities; basin arclength distinguishes two physical ones. The supplementary program independently checks exact length algebra and 7,200 direct trajectory samples.

value.rationale: The exactly solvable right-isosceles triangle is a canonical geometrically symmetric specialization of Everett’s genuine three-complete-line map. The theorem quantifies a previously qualitative convergence statement via a complete finite-interval basin census, a scale-invariant exact perimeter probability, full invariant-measure simplex and coexistence of a finite-measure four-cycle physical basin with an infinite-measure fixed-point physical basin. This is a natural exact statistical invariant, not an arbitrary parameter sample or an elementary restatement of the source contraction theorem.
